fields.statement: QA cycle 2, scratch root with fake rex/claude and the branch build (go build -trimpath to a scratch path): a build workflow whose builder prompt is /design:design-critique failed at once with 'start command /design:design-critique unknown to claude: skill not installed; run rhiza guide install --agent claude' and an inbox item naming rhiza run resume --retry while the plugin was absent; after writing plugins/cache/mkt/design/1.0.0/skills/design-critique/SKILL.md under HOME/.claude, rhiza run resume --foreground --retry launched the builder as attempt 1 (fake builder logged 'alpha 1') and the inbox emptied, so the cycle-1 plugin finding is fixed. go test -trimpath ./internal/adapter/... and TestScripts/run-start-skill-missing passed.

QA cycle 2, scratch root, branch build: an accepted change set, the user guide missing rhiza-builder and made read-only; two rhiza daemon --once --autonomous polls logged 'could not refresh the user guide ...: permission denied', started no run and left exactly one guide-stale inbox item naming the scope, the error and rhiza guide install --agent claude. After chmod u+w the next poll refreshed the guide, started the ship-change run and the guide-stale item was gone. A workflow starting with a non-Rhiza plugin command (/design:design-critique) is not gated, as only skills the guide ships are checked. go test -trimpath ./internal/api/ -run 'DaemonGuide|HealthGuide|StartNotSubmitted' passed.

QA cycle 2, scratch HOME with the branch build: rhiza health listed guide right after usage, warn 'an installed guide is out of date' with next rhiza guide install --agent claude after skills/rhiza-verifier was removed, and ok '1 installed guide(s) current' after guide install. The command's exit 1 came from the scratch repo's own failing check part, not the guide part.

QA cycle 2, scratch root, branch build: with a writable user guide missing rhiza-builder, rhiza daemon --once logged 'refreshed the user guide ... to <running version>' before starting the ship-change run, and skills/rhiza-builder was back in place; with the folder read-only it logged a failed refresh and changed nothing.
